title: Split the new-pane button into New Terminal and New Claude
notes:
The title row's '+ New pane' becomes two halves: [New Terminal | New Claude]. New Terminal is today's button and the terminal-add key. New Claude opens a new worker pane showing a Claude screen like main's, in the project's folder, empty and waiting for the first prompt.

Keyboard first: New Claude gets its own key, a row in src/shared/keys/actions.ts beside terminal-add (a terminals-scope name), and src/renderer/keys/help.ts plus the terminals blurb say so. Both halves keep the button's mousedown preventDefault, so a click leaves the keyboard where it was; the new pane takes it once it opens, as addPane does now.

Two costs, both part of this card:
1. A screen with no first prompt. Today a worker screen only comes from pane run --screen with a prompt (workers-decision-5, screen-workers.ts). New Claude needs a path that opens the pane as a screen and starts nothing until the user types. It should run in the screen host like a worker screen, so it outlives an app restart (workers-decision-6; Windows has no host, so there the turn ends with the app).
2. A screen opened by hand is the user's, not main's worker. The worker-screen refusals of /clear, /resume, /branch and /rewind do not apply to it, and it reports to nobody when its turn ends (workers README: 'a Claude opened by hand tells nobody'). The rule saying which screen is which goes in a small module with a test (workflow-rule-2), and the refusal's predicate stays where the refusal is decided (errors-rule-1).

After a restart it comes back as a Claude screen on the same conversation, as a worker screen does.

Docs: workers and panes README, a decision entry for the hand-opened screen, history.
